title: Auto Loans: Amount of a Bank-Error Returned Payment Fee Waiver
content:
How much is waived when PCB corrects a returned payment fee on an Auto Loans account as its own error, and where the waived sum lands, is fixed here.

## Rule

- The sum waived is the full fee, to the cent; a returned payment fee is never waived in part.
- Nothing is waived when a fee waiver naming that fee already exists on the loan's activity.
- Nothing is waived when PCB error is not established for the payment behind the fee.
- Of the sum waived, any part that had already been settled out of a payment goes to principal as of the waiver date; the remainder reduces fees due.

## Condition, judgement, outcome

| PCB error established | Earlier waiver naming the fee | Sum waived |
|---|---|---|
| yes | none | the whole fee |
| yes | exists | nothing |
| no | none | nothing |
| no | exists | nothing |

## Illustrations (invented fees)

- A returned payment fee of 25.00, unpaid, qualifies: 25.00 is waived, all of it reducing fees due, with 0.00 applied to principal.
- The same fee, already paid out of a later payment, qualifies: 25.00 is waived and applied to principal on the waiver date.
- The fee already has a waiver: nothing further is waived.
